judged_text: expandable_first_post? silently drops the "an embeddable host is configured" gate that the original intent of the check encoded — it now returns true whenever embed_truncate is on and the topic has an embed, even if the embeddable_hosts table is empty or the host was deleted after the topic was embedded. A site that removes all embeddable hosts keeps serving truncated/expandable first posts for previously-embedded topics (the check no longer consults current host configuration), a behavior change from the prior contract that the renamed spec case ('is false if embeddable_host is blank' now passes vacuously with no host fabrication) papers over rather than explicitly accepts.

A site that removes all embeddable hosts keeps serving truncated/expandable first posts for previously-embedded topics (the check no longer consults current host configuration), a behavior change from the prior contract that the renamed spec case ('is false if embeddable_host is blank' now passes vacuously with no host fabrication) papers over rather than explicitly accepts.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic.rb, `expandable_first_post?` changed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to just `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, with no replacement check against the new `EmbeddableHost` table. This makes the predicate return true for already-embedded topics whenever `embed_truncate` is enabled, even if there are currently zero allowed hosts (or they were deleted). The updated spec also no longer actually asserts the previous “no hosts configured => false” behavior because it doesn’t set `embed_truncate` true and doesn’t stub `has_topic_embed?` true in that case, so it can pass vacuously.
